# Exact upper faces and failure of independent patch-budget allocation

This note computes the minimal upper faces at the four terminal roots in the actual eight-base homothetic example. It also verifies a revised positive concave radius profile for which every terminal-root face's independent weighted Helly guarantee is below one quarter of the total mass. Neither conclusion is an OC counterexample.

Use the base indices and original lifted heights from candidate 588eabf65d9a1440:

| index | base | original height |
|---|---|---:|
| 0 | \((-1,-2)\) | 8 |
| 1 | \((-1,-1)\) | 11 |
| 2 | \((-1,0)\) | 14 |
| 3 | \((0,0)\) | 16 |
| 4 | \((0,1)\) | 12 |
| 5 | \((0,2)\) | 8 |
| 6 | \((1,2)\) | 10 |
| 7 | \((2,3)\) | 8 |

The roots are \(1,2,3,4\), and the nonroot-to-parent edges are \(0\to1,\ 5\to4,\ 6\to4,\ 7\to6\), with respective partners \(2,3,2,4\).

## 1. Upper-face incidence and complete projected lattice sets

The three upper facets of the convex hull of the lifted graph have index sets

\[
F_1=\{0,1,2,3\},\qquad
F_2=\{2,3,4,5,6,7\},\qquad
F_3=\{0,3,7\}.
\]

Their supporting upper planes are exactly the three affine functions in the original profile. Their projected polygons are respectively the triangle \((0,2,3)\), the quadrilateral \((2,3,7,5)\), and the triangle \((0,3,7)\). Each displayed index set is the complete set of integer points in its projected polygon.

At a graph point, “minimal upper face” here means the smallest face containing that point which admits a supporting normal with positive height coefficient. Vertical base supports can be added to an upper support without losing that positive coefficient. Consequently the terminal-root minimal faces are:

| terminal root | minimal upper face | projected dimension | relative Helly number |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| 1 | \(E=\{0,1,2\}\) | 1 | 2 |
| 2 | \(\{2\}\) | 0 | 1 |
| 3 | \(\{3\}\) | 0 | 1 |
| 4 | \(F=F_2=\{2,3,4,5,6,7\}\) | 2 | 3 |

For root 1 the vertical left-base support and \(F_1\) expose the edge \(E\). Root 2 is a vertex exposed using the left-base support and upper facets. Root 3 is the common vertex of the three upper facets. Root 4 is in the relative interior of \(F_2\).

The two maximal selected faces cover the entire graph, and

\[
E\cap F=\{2\}.
\]

The quadrilateral's exact base inequalities are

\[
y\ge0,\quad 2y-3x\ge0,\quad 2y-x\le4,\quad y-2x\le2.
\]

Enumerating their integer solutions gives exactly \(2,3,4,5,6,7\).

For \(h(F)=3\), the triangle \(\{2,3,4\}\) gives a three-set deletion-hull witness. The only convex-position four-subsets of \(F\) are

\[
\{2,3,5,6\},\qquad \{2,3,5,7\}.
\]

Both have point 4 in the intersection of all four deletion hulls. For the first, point 4 is the common midpoint of diagonals \((2,6)\) and \((3,5)\). For the second,

\[
p_4=\tfrac23p_2+\tfrac13p_7=\tfrac12p_3+\tfrac12p_5.
\]

There are no larger convex-position subsets. This proves the upper bound three: witnesses for a minimal finite family with empty \(F\)-intersection would form a convex-position subset whose deletion hulls have no point of \(F\). Exact determinant enumeration in the verifier checks the exhaustive subset assertion.

The graph union has **exactly** Helly number five. The old five-point deletion-hull witness gives the lower bound. The general union inequality \(h(E\cup F)\le h(E)+h(F)\) gives the upper bound: when a family misses both sets, select at most the respective Helly numbers of members to witness each failure, then take their union. Thus one cannot subtract one from these Helly costs merely because the two faces share a graph vertex.

## 2. The original weights are paid by the planar face

For the original radius \(r_i=R+t_i/8\), set \(s=R+1\). Apart from the common volume of the reference simplex,

\[
W_F-3W_{P\setminus F}
=[(s+1)^d-(s+3/8)^d]
+[(s+3/4)^d-(s+3/8)^d]
+[(s+1/2)^d-(s+3/8)^d]
+[(s+1/4)^d-s^d]>0.
\]

This holds for every \(R\ge0\) and \(d\ge1\), term by term. Therefore \(W_F/3>T/4\). In the earlier \(R=1,d=2\) integer units,

\[
W_E=1101,\quad W_F=2296,\quad W_{E\cap F}=484,\quad T=2913.
\]

Weighted Doignon on the affine face graph \(F\), followed by ordinary Grünbaum fiber by fiber, suffices for this particular original family in every dimension.

## 3. A compatible profile that defeats every independent patch bound

Keep the same base polygon and take \(d=1\) with interval fibers \([0,r(z)]\), where

\[
r(z)=\min\{1+z_2/4,\ 17/25-(8/25)z_1\}.
\]

This gives the exact radii, in units \(1/100\),

\[
(50,75,100,68,68,68,36,4).
\]

Both affine functions are positive at the polygon vertices where they determine the minimum; the minimum is \(1/25>0\). The hypograph defines an actual full-dimensional compact convex body. Passing to the hull of its eight full fibers preserves those fibers and their positive lattice support.

All four exact midpoint identities remain true. The parity roots are \(2,1,3,4\); root 3 ties point 5 in radius, and is the unique smaller-norm choice in that parity class. The other roots are strict maxima.

If \(\widetilde t_i=100r_i\), the new graph is the invertible affine image of the original graph given by

\[
\widetilde t=(76-274z_1+100z_2+25t)/7.
\]

Its positive height coefficient preserves the upper-face incidence. Thus all face sets and Helly numbers above remain exactly the same.

The new masses in units \(1/100\) are

\[
W_E=225,\quad W_F=344,\quad W_{E\cap F}=100,\quad T=469.
\]

Even giving each patch its entire overlap mass, the largest of the four terminal-root-face guarantees is

\[
\max\{225/2,\ 100,\ 68,\ 344/3\}=344/3<469/4.
\]

The exact gap is \(31/12\) in these integer units, or \(31/1200\) in actual interval mass. Assigning the shared atom only once cannot improve either independent guarantee. Hence the proposed independent allocation by \(W_{\rm face}/h({\rm face})\) is insufficient even in an actual positive concave homothetic family with the canonical terminating parity forest.

This is not failure of the desired actual depth. At graph point 4, the disjoint midpoint pairs \((3,5)\) and \((2,6)\) give counted weight at least

\[
68+\min(68,68)+\min(100,36)=172>469/4.
\]

Ordinary interval Grünbaum then proves an actual normalized depth of at least \(86/469>1/8\). The missing ingredient in the failed independent-patch allocation is a joint use of the compatible graph relations, rather than a reduction of either individual face's Helly number.

The exact standard-library verifier is verify_eight_base_upper_faces_and_patch_budget.py.
